text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:

- Leading Swiss parties want to complete bilateral negotiations with the European Union on trade and other ties as soon as possible. But the parties also backed government stances that have helped slow the talks, including demands that trans-Alpine goods traffic be shunted from the roads to the railway.

- British TV station BBC said Swiss gold coins might have been produced with Nazi victims' gold. But the Swiss Finance Ministry said the gold used to mint so-called Vreneli coins came from Swiss National Bank stocks that pre-dated World War Two.
- The financial situation of most Swiss cantons is unsatisfactory as total spending in 1996 rose by 4.5 percent from the year before while income remained stable.

- Swiss pharma giant Novartis trimmed the number of research projects inherited from the fusion of Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz by 10 to total 75. But analysts say the portfolio still stands up to comparison with the group's international competitors.
- Representatives of the Vaudt cantonal government citizised the Swiss government for planning to deport most Bosnians who came as refugees during the Yugoslav wars.
- Migros, Switzerland's biggest supermarket and retail chain, will start accepting credit cards after refusing for decades because of the commissions.
- In an unusually emotional debate, the upper house of parliament on Tuesday voted in favour of a law proposal, which will lead to a more restrictive unemloyment policy.
